title: Compactification of an affine scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme of finite type over a field $K$. There
is an open dense immersion $X\to\bar X$ with $\bar X$ projective
over $K$ (choose a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_K$, take the scheme-theoretic closure in $\mathbf P^n_K$); one
has $\kundim\bar X=\kundim X$.

proof.text: Use exists_finset_closure_range_appTop_union_eq_top for the affine finite-type structure map to obtain a finite set s of global sections generating the coordinate ring over the base. Put n = Option s and i = none. The function on {k : n // k ≠ i} given by some a ↦ a has range exactly s, also when s is empty. AffineSpace.isClosedImmersion_homOfVector gives the closed immersion e, and AffineSpace.homOfVector_over gives its compatibility with the structure map. Compose e with the inverse standard chart isomorphism and the open inclusion to define j; it is an immersion. This directly implements the polynomial presentation in the source, without the more general exists_isImmersion_projectiveSpace interface, which does not retain e.

source.place: Proof, first two sentences: finite generators, polynomial presentation, and the standard affine chart

proof.text: The affine scheme X is quasi-compact, and finite projective space over Spec K is separated and therefore quasi-separated. Thus quasiCompact_of_compactSpace makes j quasi-compact. Apply [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] to j: Mathlib supplies IsOpenImmersion j.toImage and IsDominant j.toImage. The latter gives DenseRange j.toImage directly. The image inclusion j.imageι is a closed immersion by construction. No separate sheaf-injectivity argument or quasi-compactness proof for j.toImage is needed.

source.place: Tag 01RG, lemma-quasi-compact-immersion; Mathlib Morphisms/Immersion.lean:259 and IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean:720

proof.text: Equip j.image with the K-structure morphism j.imageι followed by the projective-space projection. The closed immersion j.imageι itself witnesses IsHProjective for this map, using the finite coordinate type n. An H-projective morphism is proper, so this structure map is locally of finite type and quasi-compact.

source.place: Proof, closed subscheme hence projective sentence

proof.text: Apply the dense-open clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] to j.toImage into the finite-type K-scheme j.image, and reverse the equality. This gives topologicalKrullDim j.image = topologicalKrullDim X. All constructions and the dimension theorem include empty schemes, and n has the distinguished element none even when the generator set is empty.
